carrierPolicy: OpenCode 1 lists both possible literals; V4 real-host preflight must pin exactly one. This matrix authorizes no profile.
evidenceNotes: V4 denotes the real-host profile preflight before a validation run. In retained evidence quotations, MC means Magic Context, OC2 means OpenCode 2, and compartments are persisted summaries of conversation ranges. ck-mc names the Rust Magic Context module carrier. Quotations retain the original wording and source-scope qualifications; they are historical evidence, not fresh runtime attestations.

The owner hydrated opencode-zen-free-historian-evidence.json because opencode-zen-historian-tools-evidence.json was not retained. Its recorded requests pin the three Zen ids; they are not inferred from display names.
Null settings, variants and tariffs with source unknown are unresolved, not effective null reports or claims of zero cost. V4 preflight must pin them or drop the row before a validation run.
The OMP cline-pass catalog is unavailable after revocation of the Cline grant. No OpenRouter or Zen Muse id is substituted.
Plain pi has no evidence-backed candidate; no ck-mc carrier is an activation target. Dropped rows remain in the inventory but must not be sent.

tariffSource.quote: The two grid lanes use separate host roots; live provider requests are native and direct to `https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions` for DeepSeek/GLM/MiMo and to the native `https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/responses` endpoint for Muse (158 and 34 observed requests respectively). Successful response bodies and compartment contents are not exported. Usage is exported both from MC accounting and from per-assistant-step host counters; tools and step counts come from host stores without arguments. The host sums, not MC's potentially last-step-only OC2 historian collection, are used for the cost tables. Timeout rows show only known partial usage. Context/output caps apply per request, not to cumulative input across tool loops, repairs or fallback passes. HTTP errors are verbatim. Free-tier catalog prices are zero; reported token counts measure work, not paid account charges or a trustworthy estimate of latency.
